data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 argues against decentralization by claiming coordination decay causes slow patch propagation, but its causal mechanism conflates 'decentralized operation' with 'slow deployment.' A large monolithic service also has staged rollout, change-control windows, and canary requirements that delay global patching; conversely, a decentralized network of small services can employ automated push-based update mechanisms with per-operator opt-out, producing faster effective patching than a risk-averse monolith. The argument does not establish that operational independence causally implies slower remediation.
